extraction.name: MINT-1T
extraction.description: MINT-1T is the largest and most diverse open-source multimodal interleaved dataset to date, comprising one trillion text tokens and 3.4 billion images, a 10x scale-up from existing open-source datasets. It includes previously untapped sources such as PDFs and ArXiv papers in addition to HTML documents. The final dataset contains 922 billion HTML tokens, 93B PDF tokens, and 9B ArXiv tokens across 1054 million documents.
extraction.creator: University of Washington, Salesforce Research, Stanford University, University of Texas at Austin, University of California Berkeley
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from CommonCrawl WARC dumps (HTML documents from May 2017 to April 2024), CommonCrawl WAT files (PDF documents from February 2023 to April 2024), and ArXiv LaTeX source code. HTML documents were extracted by parsing DOM trees, PDFs were downloaded and parsed using PyMuPDF to extract reading order, and ArXiv documents were built from LaTeX source using TexSoup. The data processing utilized an average of 2,350 CPU cores and approximately 4.2M CPU hours.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CommonCrawl WARC files (May 2017 to April 2024) for HTML documents, CommonCrawl WAT files (February 2023 to April 2024) for PDF documents, and ArXiv LaTeX source code.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data collection ran from January 2024 to June 2024. Web data spans from 2013 to 2024 (HTML: May 2017 - April 2024; PDFs: February 2023 - April 2024).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Email addresses were anonymized with templates like 'email@example.com' and IP addresses were replaced with randomly generated non-functional IPs. For PDFs, reading order was determined by clustering text block bounding boxes based on columns and ordering from top left to bottom right, with images anchored based on proximity to text blocks. For ArXiv, LaTeX code was cleaned by removing imports, bibliography, tables, and citation tags; input tags were replaced with file contents for multi-file papers.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text quality filtering: non-English documents were removed using Fasttext language identification (confidence threshold 0.65); URLs with NSFW substrings were removed; RefinedWeb filters removed documents with excessive duplicate n-grams or those identified as low quality by MassiveText rules. Image filtering: images smaller than 150 pixels or larger than 20,000 pixels were removed; HTML images with aspect ratio > 2 were removed, and PDF images with aspect ratio > 3 were removed. Safety filtering: NSFW image detector was applied and documents with any NSFW image were discarded; PII (emails, IPs) was anonymized. Deduplication: Bloom Filter for paragraph/document text deduplication (false positive rate 0.01, 13-gram paragraphs); documents with >80% duplicate paragraphs were discarded; exact paragraph deduplication on 2% of each CommonCrawl snapshot to remove boilerplate; image deduplication via SHA256 hashes removed images appearing >10 times within a snapshot. PDFs >50MB or >50 pages were discarded.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: NSFW image detector (https://github.com/GantMan/nsfw_model), Fasttext language identification, PyMuPDF for PDF parsing, TexSoup for ArXiv parsing, Bloom Filter (bff) for deduplication, GPT-2 tokenizer for token counting, Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and GPT-4 for domain classification analysis.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be maintained by the authors through the Huggingface interface. Updates will be communicated through the README. Older versions will be accessible through the Git history. Contributions will be accepted through Pull Requests. Users can submit removal requests via a Google form.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset is sourced from the public web and may contain images of individuals and text about specific individuals. Personally identifiable information such as email addresses and IP addresses were masked (emails replaced with template 'email@example.com' and IPs replaced with random non-functional IPs). NSFW/pornographic images were filtered out. Sensitive data potentially present on the public web (race, ethnicity, religious beliefs, political opinions, health data) may still be found.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors acknowledge the importance of avoiding exposure of harmful content from the web. They take measures to filter PII and NSFW content. They note that MINT-1T was built to make research into large multimodal models more accessible, and inappropriate use cases include training models to ingest or generate PII or sensitive content, as well as military applications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors avoid using model-based heuristics for text filtering as they have been shown to favor text from certain demographics. Analysis shows OBELICS is concentrated in 'Humanities and Social Sciences' domain, while MINT-1T HTML subset has broader domain representation and MINT-1T PDF subset has higher proportion of 'Science and Technology' documents.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include: (1) PyMuPDF sometimes fails to detect images in PDFs; (2) PDFs have arbitrary layouts leading to incorrect reading order extraction (e.g., reading across column boundaries); (3) the dataset is not self-contained and relies on external image URLs that may suffer from link rot; (4) the dataset is over 300TB, making full hosting infeasible; (5) the dataset may still contain confidential or offensive content despite filtering. Inappropriate uses include training models that generate PII or sensitive content and military applications.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MINT-1T is designed for pre-training large multimodal models that can process multiple interleaved images and text. It can also be used for generating interleaved image-text sequences or building multimodal document retrieval systems. In the paper, it was used for training (4.6B multimodal models trained on 10B multimodal tokens with a 50/50 mixture of image-text captioning and multimodal interleaved batches).
